about: Google Photos' colour tools, read as lookup tables. colour-tables.png at the repository root holds the tables themselves; this is how they were made and how well the app reproduces them.
source: Google Photos on the web (photos.google.com), 2026-09-25, through google-web.mjs; copies come back as 1000px JPEGs. The web editor is the same engine as the Android app: Saturation +100 from a Galaxy S23 Ultra (Photos 7.93) and from the web agreed to a median of 1.4 levels over 729 colours.

charts.9: lut-chart.mjs 9: 729 patches, levels round(k x 255/8), mostly between the 13's. Held out: never in the tables.
charts.13: lut-chart.mjs 13: 2197 flat patches filling 2160 square, levels round(k x 255/12). The tables.

read: lut-measure.mjs: the mean of the middle 40% of each patch. Less the capture's one bias, clipped JPEG noise at the ends of the range (white read 1.53 low, black 0.40 high, on colours Skin tone does not touch; every other level within 0.10), undone in colour-tables.mjs.

global.about: The same 9³ colours with the grid filling the frame, and in the middle half on black and on white, at +100: median / 90th percentile / worst difference between the two, in levels. Within the capture's noise for every tool, so none of them looks at the rest of the photo.

noise: Two readings of the same colour, one off each chart: 0.85 levels apart on average, but those colours are mostly 0 and 255 where the noise clips. Between them a reading is about 1.1 levels from the truth: colours Skin tone leaves alone read 1.09 from where they started on the 9³ chart and 1.25 on the 13³.

app.about: The app's 2160 PNG exports of the same charts (ours.mjs), against Google's copies, in levels of RGB distance: mean / 90th percentile / worst. chart is the 13³ chart over all ten settings, which is the tables' own colours; heldOut100 is the 9³ chart at +100 (Tint's on black), which the tables never saw; moved100 is how far Google moved those on average. perKnot is the 13³ chart setting by setting.

open: The worst held-out colours, 13 to 25 levels, are at the edge of Skin tone's and Blue tone's bands and where Contrast and Saturation push a colour into the end of the range: both bend between the chart's colours. A 9³ table predicts the 13³ colours about as well as the 13³ table predicts the 9³, so the mean is set by the capture's noise, not the grid; only the band edges would gain from a finer one.
Google's order when tools are combined is not known: every capture was one tool at a time. The app runs them in the order Google lists them.
